issues.detail: The Greek 'δι ους' (for/because of the people) is rendered as 'vì nó' (because of it), which shifts the focus from the people to the land/rain, changing the logic of who the vegetation is intended for.

The Greek 'πολλακις' (many times/frequently) is rendered as 'thường xuyên' (regularly). While similar, the Greek emphasizes the repetitive action of the rain, but the primary issue is the misplacement of the purpose of the vegetation.
